statements.status_notes: Apache Airflow 3.3.2 resolves the caller from an explicit Authorization bearer token whenever one is presented, and uses the session cookie only when there is none (https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/72225, backported to the 3.3 line in https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/72723; announcement https://lists.apache.org/thread/3p7zpdvv40tn01m0xk5mt2rxg88mw8w1). The advisory affects only Airflow 3.3.0 and 3.3.1, and no earlier Airflow release was published as this package. Each of the 110 airflow packages published for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository (3.3.0-0 to 3.4.0-14, amd64 and arm64) was placed by what it installs, read from the package's own file list and md5sums: 3.3.0-0 to 3.3.0-3 install apache-airflow-core 3.3.0 and 3.3.1-0 to 3.3.1-15 install 3.3.1, and are affected; 3.3.2-0 to 3.3.2-19 install 3.3.2 and 3.4.0-0 to 3.4.0-14 install 3.4.0. In the unpacked 3.3.2-0 and 3.4.0-0 packages, get_user in airflow/api_fastapi/core_api/security.py returns the user from the bearer credential before anything else; in the unpacked 3.3.0-0 and 3.3.1-1 packages, get_user first returns the user that the cookie-refresh middleware cached on the request and reads the bearer token only when there is none. Every other build's copy of the file has the same md5 as the unpacked build of its Airflow release, on both architectures. 3.3.2-0 is the first published package with the fix.
